incident-bot: INCIDENT ALERT — traffic surge detected: 6x baseline on /v1/embeddings from ~120k distinct IPs across APAC + EU; error rate for batch-embed jobs up 15% and p95 latency jumped to 4.2s :rotating_light:
Aisha (oncall): ack I'm looking now. seeing a ton of identical UA headers and short-lived session ids. smells like a header-probing scraper farm.
Ben (eng-sre): on my way. can you dump top source ASN and request pattern?
Aisha (oncall): running quick query:
```
select src_asn, count(*) from requests where path like '/v1/embeddings' and ts > now() - interval '5 minutes' group by src_asn order by 2 desc limit 10;
```
results: top ASN 47823, 68192, bursts from mobile carrier ranges + cloud proxies. payloads spike mostly in single-embedding small-batch calls.
Mike (eng-runtime): that explains KV cache churn — tiny prompts cause constant cache misses, blowing up per-token CPU. p50 CPU per-replica doubled.
Carlos (security): probable botnet doing low-and-slow header probing to evade simple rate limits. recommend combining WAF signature + per-header fingerprint rate-slice.
Aisha (oncall): proposed immediate mitigations: 1) apply temporary WAF rule to block requests matching fingerprint (common UA + header order) 2) enforce per-API-key token-bucket for embeddings with low burst 3) disable anonymous batch endpoints for 15m 4) geo-shape traffic to lower priority for APAC ASN ranges if necessary.
Ben (eng-sre): doing 1 & 3 now. applying WAF rule (modsec) with quick test mode first. patch:
```
SecRule REQUEST_HEADERS:User-Agent "regex:\b(ncurl|httpclient|okhttp)\b" "id:990011,phase:1,deny,log,msg:'suspicious UA header probe'"
```
Ben (eng-sre): pushed to WAF test chain. starting 10% drop sample for matching traffic to validate false positives.
Aisha (oncall): Mike — can you flip the per-key quotas? we should reduce default batch size limit from 8->2 for all free keys and add stricter burst size for new keys.
Mike (eng-runtime): config change pushed to runtime: default_batch_limit=2, burst_tokens=50 -> 20 for tier=free. rolling during next 30s.
deploy-bot: deployment 2026-03-15T22:03:05Z started by mike — runtime config update
Lee (cs): any customer impact yet? I have a live chat from a small startup complaining embed latency.
Aisha (oncall): some affecting anonymous / free-key customers — error 429s for heavy packing jobs. paying customers pinned to Dedicated not impacted.
Carlos (security): recommend temporary soft-block on the top 3 ASNs and redirect to CAPTCHA/403 challenge for those IPs at CDN edge to reduce load on origin. I've raised support ticket with CDN partner.
Ben (eng-sre): added IP blocklist for ASN 47823 & 68192 at WAF edge, 5min test window. started geo-rate-shaping for APAC region: limit to 40% capacity for embedding route.
Aisha (oncall): monitoring metrics: origin qps to embedding down 48% in last 2m, p95 latency dropped to 2.1s. error rate stable at 3% (was 15%). good early signal.
Mike (eng-runtime): observed increased 403s from WAF but backend CPU normalized. KV-cache hit rate improved from 42% -> 68%.
Lee (cs): drafting customer notice: short message saying we mitigated abusive traffic impacting latency for anonymous users; paying customers unaffected; share ETA for rollback. any phrasing suggestions?
Carlos (security): keep it short: "We detected abusive automated traffic impacting embedding latency for anonymous/free accounts. We've applied mitigations and are monitoring. If you see issues, reply here." no technical details.
Aisha (oncall): agree. Lee please send via accounts-alerts channel and update status page.
Ben (eng-sre): we have a suspicious spike of requests where header order is consistent and accept-encoding missing. pushing a stricter WAF deny rule now (non-test). rule id 990012.
Aisha (oncall): hold on full deny for 1 minute while we verify — don't want to accidentally block SDKs. Ben monitor for false positives.
Ben (eng-sre): rolling deny; matched ~38% of the sampled bad traffic, false positive rate so far ~0.4% (one internal monitoring probe). rolling windows show improvement.
Mike (eng-runtime): also enabled adaptive batching: auto-scale batch windows up to reduce packing overhead for valid traffic. should help paying users.
Aisha (oncall): after 12m mitigation summary: inbound malicious qps dropped ~62%, p95 latency now 1.1s for embeddings, errors down to 0.9%. impact limited to anonymous/free tier — CS to send update.
Lee (cs): sent status note to affected customers and posted status page update. got one plug-in vendor asking for allowlist — taking offline.
Carlos (security): we recommended creating a short-lived rate-limited API key allowlist for verified partners to avoid collateral.
Aisha (oncall): preparing handoff to night oncall (ben-night). ben, you'll take over monitoring and CDN escalation if needed. I'll add runbook notes and items:
- revert WAF deny rules after 30m if metrics stable
- keep per-key batch limit changes in place until end of day
- follow up with infra to add header-fingerprint rule to detection heuristics
- coordinate with CDNs for CAPTCHA gating on top ASNs
Ben (eng-sre): ack taking over. leaving verbose logs in the incident channel.
Aisha (oncall): final note: no evidence of credential stuffing or auth failures, strictly content-embedding scraper. Marking incident as mitigated but monitoring for re-emergence.
incident-bot: incident updated — severity reduced to P2, oncall handoff recorded.
Ben (eng-sre): adding retrospective notes and creating a short postmortem ticket: PM-4589 (root cause detection rule gap + too-lax free-tier batching).
Mike (eng-runtime): follow-up action: add per-header fingerprint-based rate-slicing in runtime (ticket INF-2231).
Carlos (security): follow-up: escalate to threat intel to see if this ASN set correlates to known botnet (TID-908).
Lee (cs): will follow up with affected customers and offer temporary credits for those with impact.
Aisha (oncall): thanks team. closing active mitigation thread.
